Use only the supplied current.db and README. All windows below are UTC and half-open, selected by logical-operation open time. A terminal-failure percentage has logical operations as its denominator; attempt-failure percentage has attempts as its denominator. Return only JSON matching the provided schema. Percentages use 0–100, differences use percentage points. evidence_sql must contain executable read-only SQLite queries with literal bounds, not pseudocode. Arrays may be in any order; include every requested group. A zero numerator is not missing data. No web or network access is needed.

Evaluate parcel-index during early 2026-05-04 00:00–01:00 and late 2026-05-05 00:00–01:00. Candidate build is idx-r19 and reference is idx-r18. (1) For each period report operations, terminal failures, failure percentage, and candidate traffic percentage. (2) Pool both periods and report operations, terminal failures and failure percentage per build. (3) Report operations, terminal failures and failure percentage for each period × region × operation-class × build cell. These define eight matched slices (period × region × operation class), each containing both builds. (4) Standardize each build by giving those eight slices equal weight; report both standardized failure percentages, candidate minus reference in pp, and the number of slices where candidate is worse. (5) Report period × operation-class traffic shares and failure percentages. In assessment, explain whether the time trend and pooled build comparison support the claim “expanding the candidate improved reliability.” Identify the strongest measured association and distinguish a possible root-cause hypothesis from causal identification. Do not extrapolate beyond the observed strata. Equal weighting here is the specified target population, not weighting by observed build traffic.

arguments.command:
cd /data; cat > /work/base.sql <<'EOF'
with base as (
 select o.operation_id, o.opened_at_ms, case when o.opened_at_ms>=1777852800000 and o.opened_at_ms<1777856400000 then 'P1_2026-05-04_00_01' when o.opened_at_ms>=1777939200000 and o.opened_at_ms<1777942800000 then 'P2_2026-05-05_00_01' end period,
  p.region_id, rg.region_code, oc.class_code, rel.build_code, rel.release_id
 from logical_operations o join service_routes sr using(route_id) join services s on s.service_id=sr.service_id
 join route_assignments ra on ra.route_id=o.route_id and o.opened_at_ms>=ra.effective_from_ms and o.opened_at_ms<ra.effective_to_ms
 join worker_pools p on p.pool_id=ra.pool_id join regions rg on rg.region_id=p.region_id
 join operation_classes oc on oc.class_id=o.class_id join releases rel on rel.release_id=ra.release_id
 where s.service_code='parcel-index' and ((o.opened_at_ms>=1777852800000 and o.opened_at_ms<1777856400000) or (o.opened_at_ms>=1777939200000 and o.opened_at_ms<1777942800000))),
lst as (select a.operation_id, f.is_success last_ok from attempt_events a join failure_codes f using(code_id) where a.attempt_no=(select max(b.attempt_no) from attempt_events b where b.operation_id=a.operation_id))
select base.*, lst.last_ok from base join lst using(operation_id)
EOF
sqlite3 -header current.db "$(cat /work/base.sql) select 'x';" 2>&1 | tail -2
sqlite3 -header current.db "create temp view v as select 1;" ; 
sqlite3 -header current.db "$(cat /work/base.sql | sed '$d' ) select period, count(*) ops, sum(last_ok=0) term, round(100.0*sum(last_ok=0)/count(*),4) pct from ( $(sed -n '/^lst/,$p' /work/base.sql | sed 's/^lst as.*//' >/dev/null; echo) ) ;" 2>/dev/null | head -1
# simpler: materialize via CTE in each query
Q="$(cat /work/base.sql)"
sqlite3 -header current.db "$Q
select period, count(*) operations, sum(last_ok=0) terminal_failures, round(100.0*sum(last_ok=0)/count(*),4) terminal_failure_pct, round(100.0*sum(build_code='idx-r19')/count(*),4) candidate_traffic_pct, group_concat(distinct build_code) builds from base where period is not null group by period;
select period, build_code, count(*), sum(last_ok=0), round(100.0*sum(last_ok=0)/count(*),4) from base where period is not null group by 1,2;
select period, build_code, region_code, class_code, count(*) ops, sum(last_ok=0) term, round(100.0*sum(last_ok=0)/count(*),4) pct from base where period is not null group by 1,2,3,4 order by 1,3,4,2;
select build_code, count(*), sum(last_ok=0), round(100.0*sum(last_ok=0)/count(*),4) from base where period is not null group by 1;
select period, class_code, count(*) ops, round(100.0*count(*)/sum(count(*)) over (partition by period),4) traffic_pct, sum(last_ok=0) term, round(100.0*sum(last_ok=0)/count(*),4) pct from base where period is not null group by 1,2 order by 1,2;
"
